title: The approved Product Contract and the PRD dossier are readable on the goal

(a) The approved Product Contract dossier on the opened goal from `/product-contract/gate-1/read`: personas/journeys, requirements, criteria WITH their coverage state, assumptions, unresolved decisions, versions. (b) The document dossier on the PRD panel from `/documents/dossier/read`.

MEASURED AT HEAD (branch moe/work-2026-09-04) by architect-20a6d1eb - both reads exist DAEMON-SIDE, so this row is browser work plus decoders, not new routes:

- `/documents/dossier/read` is ALREADY in the browser's proxy roster (apps/control-room/src/live/dev-proxy-paths.ts:16); `/product-contract/gate-1/read` is NOT - so that one needs its proxy pin as well as its decoder.
- `grep -rn 'gate-1/read' apps/control-room/src` returns nothing outside the proxy list, so neither read is consumed by a screen today. That is the gap, and it is real.

THE DECODER DISCIPLINE: every live read client in apps/control-room/src/live/ decodes with an EXACT-KEY record check that REFUSES a response whose key set differs, rather than silently defaulting - a stale daemon is detected, not papered over. Follow that shape (live-sessions.ts is a compact example); a decoder that tolerates extra keys is how a shape change ships unnoticed.

CRITERIA COVERAGE STATE is the load-bearing column: the contract dossier shows each criterion WITH whether it is covered, which is what makes the screen worth opening rather than a formatted dump of the contract.
definitionOfDone: The opened goal shows the approved Product Contract dossier from `/product-contract/gate-1/read`: the approved revision id, the requirements count, and every criterion WITH its coverage state. Assert against a REAL daemon frame that a named criterion's coverage state reaches the row - a dossier that lists criteria without coverage is a formatted dump, not a dossier.
The PRD panel shows the document dossier from `/documents/dossier/read`.

Both reads have an EXACT-KEY decoder that REFUSES an unexpected key set rather than defaulting, with a test for each: a real frame decodes; a frame with an extra key is refused; a frame missing a key is refused. `/product-contract/gate-1/read` also gains its proxy pin in dev-proxy-paths.ts (`/documents/dossier/read` is already there at :16 - do not duplicate it).

Every digest mirror and roster the new decoders touch is updated together: packages generated-coverage.test.ts, apps/control-room/src/data/data-adapter.test.ts and v2/goals/approve-plan.test.tsx are the ones the parent row names - verify each by running it, and if one does not in fact pin this surface, say so in the step note rather than editing it for symmetry.
Refusals render VERBATIM with their codes on both screens - a goal whose contract read refuses must say so, not render an empty dossier that reads as 'no requirements'.

This row adds NO daemon route: `git diff --stat` shows no file under apps/daemon/src. Gates quoted with count lines: `pnpm --filter @moe/control-room test`, `pnpm typecheck`, `pnpm test` (the packages digest mirrors are touched, so the root lane is real evidence here).
taskRails: BROWSER-ONLY. Both reads are already served; this row writes decoders and screens. A daemon change means the read is not what it claims - stop and report rather than editing it.
EXACT-KEY DECODERS, matching every sibling in apps/control-room/src/live/. A tolerant decoder defeats the mechanism that detects a stale daemon.

AN EMPTY DOSSIER IS NEVER RENDERED AS EMPTINESS. A refusal renders its code; absence of data renders words saying so. The difference matters because an operator reads an empty requirements list as 'the contract has none'.
ASCII-only sources and apostrophe-free JSX text (scheduler package-boundary scan); check any new testid namespace is free; keep every production file under 250 lines.

implementationPlan.description: REFUSALS RENDER, ABSENCE IS WORDS. Both surfaces render a refusal VERBATIM with its code. And the distinction that matters: a goal whose contract read REFUSES must say so — it must NOT render an empty dossier, because an empty requirements list reads to an operator as 'this contract has no requirements', which is a different and false claim. Assert three states per surface: a real frame renders; a refusal renders its code; genuinely-absent data renders words saying it is absent. Also assert that a refusal on ONE of the two reads does not blank the OTHER.

planningNotes.approachesConsidered: REJECTED, writing a new decoder and component for `/documents/dossier/read`: both already exist (live-document-dossier.ts, preview/document-dossier.tsx) with a test and a proxy pin, and are consumed by the legacy surface — the gap is that V2 does not consume them, not that they are missing. A parallel implementation would be the exact duplication this board keeps paying for, and would leave two decoders free to disagree about the same frame. REJECTED, planning against the row's own claim that neither read is consumed: measured false for one of them, and the correction halves the work — recorded in comment-9dc32955 and re-verified in step 1. REJECTED, editing all three named digest mirrors for symmetry: DoD 4 lists them, but a mirror that does not actually pin this surface should be left alone and said so, because an edit made to satisfy a list rather than a failure quietly changes what a test asserts. REJECTED, rendering an empty dossier when a read refuses: an empty requirements list reads as 'the contract has none', which is a false claim rather than a missing one.
planningNotes.codebaseInsights: MEASURED AT HEAD (branch moe/work-2026-09-04) by architect-20a6d1eb, correcting this row's own description. THE TWO READS ARE IN DIFFERENT STATES. `/documents/dossier/read`: daemon side wired (http-listener-read-dispatch.ts:3 imports DOCUMENT_DOSSIER_PATH with its handler; document-dossier-read.ts:7 defines the path), browser decoder EXISTS (live/live-document-dossier.ts, `createLiveDocumentDossierFeed`, `LIVE_DOCUMENT_DOSSIER_LOADING`), component EXISTS (preview/document-dossier.tsx + document-dossier-state.ts), proxy pin EXISTS (dev-proxy-paths.ts:16), and it is consumed by live-app.tsx:6-20 — the LEGACY surface, reached via development-legacy-root.tsx:3 and shell-mode-view.tsx:5. `main.tsx:12` mounts v2's CordumApp, and `grep -rn 'document-dossier|DocumentDossier' apps/control-room/src/v2` = ZERO. `/product-contract/gate-1/read`: daemon side real (product-contract-gate-1-read.ts:27 path, :60 ProductContractGate1View `{outcome:"GATE", gate}` built at :113, :70-73 the refusal `{code, layer, outcome:"REFUSED"}`, :80 the port; listener imports it at http-listener-read-dispatch.ts:11-12), browser side ENTIRELY ABSENT including the proxy pin. THE DECODER DISCIPLINE to follow: every live read client uses an exact-key record check that refuses an unexpected key set rather than defaulting, so a stale daemon is detected rather than papered over.
planningNotes.risks: BIGGEST RISK — building a second dossier decoder because the row's description says neither read is consumed. It is measured false, and the duplicate would render the same frame through two decoders that can drift. Step 1 sends the worker to the correction and makes them re-run the greps. SECOND — an empty dossier standing in for a refused read: an operator reads an empty requirements list as 'the contract has none', so absence and refusal must render different words. THIRD — a tolerant gate-1 decoder: exact-key decoding is what detects a stale daemon, and a decoder that shrugs at an extra key defeats it silently; the step-6 drill forces the refusal arm to bite. FOURTH — editing the three named digest mirrors for symmetry rather than for a failure; if one does not pin this surface, touching it changes what it asserts. FIFTH — the legacy surface must keep working: it consumes the same feed, and its count line is compared against step 1's baseline. SIXTH — whether preview/document-dossier.tsx renders acceptably inside the v2 shell is genuinely unmeasured; the plan requires checking before assuming a drop-in, and adapting presentation only, never forking the feed.
